Surah al-Kawthar

Makkan, though it is said to be Madinan. Its verses are three.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words:

[1–3] ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾ ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾ [al-Kawthar: 2] ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾ [al-Kawthar: 3]

﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾: that is, abundant good from the Qur'an, wisdom, prophethood, the true religion, guidance, and what it contains of the happiness of both abodes. Ibn Jarir narrated from Abu Bishr, who said: "I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about al-Kawthar, and he said: It is the abundant good that Allah gave him. I said to Sa'id: We used to hear that it is a river in Paradise? He said: It is among the good that Allah gave him."

﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾ [al-Kawthar: 2]. The Imam said: That is, make your prayer to your Lord alone, and sacrifice your offering, which is an act of devotion to Allah alone, for He is the One who nurtures you and bestows His blessings upon you to the exclusion of any other, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: Indeed, my prayer, my rites, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-An'am: 162] ﴿He has no partner. And this I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims﴾ [al-An'am: 163]. ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾ [al-Kawthar: 3]. Ibn Jarir said: That is, your hater, O Muhammad, and your enemy is the one cut off, meaning the least, the most humiliated, the one whose line is severed and who has no descendants.

Ibn Ishaq narrated from Yazid ibn Ruman, who said: "Whenever the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was mentioned, al-'As ibn Wa'il would say: 'Leave him, for he is a man cut off, with no offspring. When he dies, his mention will end.' So Allah revealed this surah."

(p-٦٢٧٨) And from 'Ata', who said: "It was revealed concerning Abu Lahab, at the time when the son of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died. Abu Lahab went to the polytheists and said: Muhammad has been cut off tonight. So Allah revealed the surah concerning that." Shammar ibn 'Atiyyah said: It was revealed concerning 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'it. Ibn Kathir said: The verse encompasses all who are characterized by this, from among those mentioned and others.

The Imam said: The mockers from Quraysh, such as al-'As ibn Wa'il, 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'it, Abu Lahab and their like, whenever they saw the sons of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) dying, would say: "Muhammad has been cut off," meaning that no mention of him would remain in his offspring after him. They regarded this as a defect with which they would taunt him and by which they would turn people away from his followers. And whenever they saw the weakness, poverty and fewness of the Muslims, they would belittle them and minimize their affair, regarding this as a flaw in the religion, and they would take fewness and weakness as evidence that the religion is not true; for if it were true, it would have been accompanied by wealth and power, as is the way of the foolish with the truth in every age and place where ignorance prevails. The hypocrites, when they saw the hardship and distress that the believers were in, would flatter themselves with the victory of their old unbelieving brethren, and would await evil befalling the Muslims because of their small number and their empty hands of wealth. The weak among the believers who were recent in Islam would have thoughts of evil pass through their souls when the rings of hardship tightened upon them. So Allah, glorified is He, willed to purify these people's souls and to rebuke the others, in order to affirm to him the promise that He is the Victor, that his follower is the triumphant one, and that his enemy is the failed one, the cut off, whose mention will be erased and whose trace will be effaced.

Note:

Because of what has been narrated about the occasion of revelation of this surah, as we have related, the linguist Ibn Jinni went to interpret al-Kawthar as a large progeny, which is a wondrous meaning with an appropriateness to the occasion of revelation.

Ibn Jinni said in (Sharh Diwan al-Mutanabbi), in his words praising Tahir ibn al-Husayn al-'Alawi:

؎ The most manifest of the signs of al-Tihami is that he is your father, and the most beneficial of what has come to you of virtues

(p-٦٢٧٩) Among what 'Ali Abu al-Fadl al-'Arudi dictated was: "The Quraysh and the enemies of the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: Muhammad is cut off, with no offspring; when he dies, we will be rid of him. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾," meaning a large number, and you are not the cut-off one they claimed. By a large number he means progeny, and these are the children of Fatimah. Al-'Arudi said: If it is said that a person is through sons, fathers and mothers, we say: This contradicts the ruling of Allah, the Exalted, for He has said: ﴿And among his descendants: Dawud and Sulayman﴾ [al-An'am: 84], up to His words: ﴿and Yahya and 'Isa﴾ [al-An'am: 85]. Thus He made 'Isa among the offspring of Ibrahim and among his descendants, and there is no dispute that 'Isa had no father. End.

We have expanded on the proofs of the descent of the tribes (asbat) from their forefathers in the book (Sharaf al-Asbat) with what admits no addition, so refer to it.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
